auditor: Claude (independent D-10 auditor, fresh context; persona: native-level Japanese teacher, reads Vietnamese natively). Read-only on C:\src\lft-ja.
procedure: plan/prompts/P-ai-review.md step 6: random >=10 % of the lines that passed the first pass (not named in findings-answers.json / findings-language.json), threshold P0+P1 <= 2 % of audited lines, plus a re-check of 10 random fixes.

sampling.method: Line units and exclusions are in the script docstring. Ids are sorted and random.Random(20261104).sample(pop, ceil(0.1*len(pop))) is drawn for exercises, then language, then 5 fixed answer decisions, then 5 fixed language P0/P1 decisions. Exclusions: every id named in either findings file (with alsoAffects); lesson/checkpoint items whose speechItemId/writingTaskId/scenarioId is named; every line of a named reading, concept card, unit guidebook or scenario (with its ix clips); the primer intro and the two section explanations the primer findings quote. Lines that systematic generator rules changed but no finding named stay in the population.
sampling.basisForAnswerKeys: Matching read in src/lib/speech/grader.ts (whole-utterance variant by normalized form or reading, else requiredConcepts) and src/lib/writing/rubric.ts (slot variant = contiguous token run after lenient normalization and kana alignment); typed/word-bank leniency as recorded in findings-answers.json basis.

findings.problem: 'Cho tôi xem thực đơn.' The key is メニューを見せてください; alternatives are メニューをお願いします and メニューをください. メニュー、お願いします (no を) is the form the course itself teaches (コーヒー、お願いします, u0-l1-e4). It is rejected: punctuation is stripped, but a missing を is not. The first pass fixed this for 水 (u3-l2-e6) and ビール (us-l2-e5), but not here.
findings.fix: Add alternatives: メニュー、お願いします | すみません、メニューをお願いします | すみません、メニュー、お願いします. Better: a generator rule that adds 'X、お願いします' (no を) to every typed key 'Xをお願いします', with a rule-8 check. ja-vi:ud-l2-e7 (切符を1枚お願いします) should also accept 切符、1枚お願いします.

findings.problem: 'Bạn làm rơi cốc của đồng nghiệp. Hãy xin lỗi.' Speech grading matches the whole utterance and this item has no requiredConcepts. The cup has already been dropped, so the most natural apology is すみませんでした (or 申し訳ありませんでした), and it is rejected. The variants are すみません, ごめんなさい, 本当にすみません and 申し訳ありません. The first pass fixed the same gap in ja.speak.k_sorry, but not in this reserved checkpoint item.
findings.fix: Add acceptedVariants: すみませんでした | 本当にすみませんでした | 申し訳ありませんでした | あ、すみません. Also check every speech/scenario item whose target is すみません for an apology about something that already happened.

findings.problem: The instruction says 'trong phòng có một cái giường'. The bed slot has one variant, ベッドがあり, and it is matched as a contiguous token run (writing/rubric.ts containsRun). A learner who renders 'một cái' literally (部屋にベッドが一つあります / ベッドが1つあります) breaks the run and fails the slot. The answer is correct and is rejected. This is the same class of finding as ja.write.o_family (妹は二人).
findings.fix: Bed slot variants: ベッドがあり | ベッドが一つあり | ベッドが1つあり | ベッドは一つあり | ベッドは1つあり | ベッドもあり. Optional for the small slot: 部屋が小さい.

findings.problem: 'Công việc vất vả nhưng vui.' The key accepts でも and が. 仕事は大変ですけど、楽しいです is polite and correct but is rejected. けど may not be taught yet, so this is low priority.
findings.fix: Add alternatives: 仕事は大変ですけど、楽しいです | 仕事は大変ですけれど、楽しいです

findings.problem: Listening items whose audioTarget is a phone number written in digits (090-1234-5678; also um-l0-e6 080-2345-6789). Japanese reads phone numbers digit by digit (ゼロきゅうゼロの いちにさんよん…). A ja G2P/TTS front end usually reads 1234 as せんにひゃくさんじゅうよん. The clip would then teach a wrong reading and make the 1243/1234 distractor contrast unfair.
findings.fix: Give the TTS a kana or digit-by-digit audio text (e.g. ゼロきゅうゼロ、いち に さん よん、ご ろく なな はち), or check the generated clip in the ASR/CER audit before release.
findings.reason: No ja audio exists yet; this depends on how the audio session's front end normalises digits.

findings.problem: The age slot accepts 24歳 and 24さい. 二十四歳 (kanji numerals) is correct and rejected. The typed-answer numeral rule does not reach writing slots. This is rare in horizontal typing.
findings.fix: Age slot variants + 二十四歳 | 二十四さい; extend the numeral rule to writing slots.

findings.problem: The rephrase of こんにちは。隣の部屋の人ですか。 is 新しい人ですか。, which asks a different question. Said to a person's face, 新しい人 is blunt; it is normally used about a third person.
findings.fix: 隣の部屋の方ですか。 or 新しく来た人ですか。 (re-record the clip)

findings.problem: 家族は何人ですか asked to the listener is understood but plain. The idiomatic polite question is ご家族は何人ですか or 何人家族ですか.
findings.fix: ご家族は何人ですか。 || Gia đình bạn có mấy người?

findings.problem: 男のトイレはあちらです sounds crude in a polite sentence. Signs and staff say 男性用トイレ / 男子トイレ.
findings.fix: 男の人のトイレはあちらです。 || Nhà vệ sinh nam ở phía kia. (or another example: あの男は…; 男 is mostly used in compounds)

findings.problem: 雨でした。しかし、仕事はありました。 The contrast is weak ('it rained; however, there was work'), and the Vietnamese adds 'vẫn phải làm', which the Japanese does not say. It is a poor model for しかし.
findings.fix: 日本語は難しいです。しかし、おもしろいです。 || Tiếng Nhật khó. Tuy nhiên, rất thú vị.

findings.problem: 'Cái nào được?' is not idiomatic Vietnamese for どれがいいですか.
findings.fix: どれがいいですか。 || Cái nào thì được? / Bạn chọn cái nào?

findings.problem: #1 says 昨日病院へ行きました. #2 says 病院の後で…薬局へ行きます in the present. The rest of the visit is narrated in the past (呼びました, 帰りました), and #23 次の朝 is today. Read in the present, 行きます sounds like today or a habit.
findings.fix: [N] 病院の後で、トゥアンさんは近くの薬局へ行きました。 || Khám xong, Tuấn đến hiệu thuốc gần đó.

findings.problem: ナムさんはとても心配しました sits between present-tense lines (あります / 行きます). In a present narration a native writes 心配です or 心配になります.
findings.fix: [N] ナムさんはとても心配です。 || Nam rất lo lắng.

findings.problem: ごみの箱 is unidiomatic. The thing in front of a building is ごみ置き場, or ごみ箱 for a bin.
findings.fix: [N] アパートの前にごみ箱があります。 || Trước căn hộ có thùng rác. (ごみ箱 if allowed by the band; otherwise keep)

findings.problem: 同じ会社の会社員です repeats 会社. Natural: 同じ会社で働いています (働く may be above A1-1) or 同じ会社の人です.
findings.fix: [N] ランさんとナムさんは同じ会社の人です。 || Lan và Nam làm cùng một công ty.

items.note: All four suggested variants are present; lesson ja-vi:uk-l2-e2 inherits them.
Alternatives: 若いです, 彼女は若いです (key かのじょは若いです).
q2 options are now Người Việt Nam / Người Nhật / Người Hàn Quốc. With 日本の学生 and the name すずき, Người Nhật is the only answer that fits. 日本人 is not available at A1-0.
お先に失礼いたします is in uk-l1-e9 and in the variants of ja.speak.k_osaki, so uk-l2-e1 and uk-l3-e2 have it too.
The alternatives list わたしは / 私は with both へ and に, and both word orders.
The goal says chị Tanaka. All six ix_call_sick clips are voice A (female).
p0.rephraseText, r0.text and the clip all read 今日はどんなごようですか。 Polite and right for a clerk. The audio still has to be generated.
九百円 / 七百円 / 四百円: run-time furigana gives きゅうひゃく, ななひゃく, よんひゃく, all correct (no rendaku/gemination with these numerals).
お父さんの誕生日に、時計を買います。 is natural ('for father's birthday'). #20 お父さんの誕生日ですか stays consistent.

Japanese and Vietnamese now agree (何もわかりません / Chẳng biết gì cả), and the line reads as 'I have no idea what's going on'. In a dark room a native would still say 何もみえません (kana, as the JLPT reading already does). Not counted as a finding.

summary.line: 407 lines audited (118 exercise, 289 language): P0 3, P1 0, P2 12 -> P0+P1 = 0.74 % of audited lines, under the 2 % threshold: PASS. Fix re-check: 10/10 correct.
caveats: On its own, the answer-key stratum is 3/118 = 2.54 %, above 2 %. The rule is applied to all audited lines, as in the en-vi and it-vi audits. With only 3 hits the estimate is wide: a 95 % interval runs from about 0.5 % to 7 %.

All three P0s belong to the first pass's main class: a correct learner answer rejected for a missing variant. Each is a sibling the systematic rules did not reach: 'X、お願いします' without を, a past-tense apology (すみませんでした) in speech, and a counted object (一つ) in a writing slot. A generator rule for each, with a rule-8 check, would close the class better than three point fixes.
The language sample found no P0/P1. Its 9 findings are style or naturalness notes (P2), concentrated in story narration tense and lexicon examples, which the first pass read only one third of.

Not covered: audio (none generated for ja), running the app, Hán-Việt entries, story questions. Scenario lines are thin in the sample: 2 drawn, because the 8 named scenarios were excluded whole. The primer is thin too: 2 lines drawn.
Lines were judged one at a time. Story lines were read with the previous and next sentence, and comprehension items with their full clip or reading text.
